title: Few-shot ordering perturbation chronicle
content:
Purpose: quick-running personal notebook to catalog how exemplar ordering (and small perturbations) affects model outputs for classification-style few-shot prompts. Want a compact decision matrix for when to randomize, when to anchor, and quick heuristics for shipping template defaults.

Motivation / hypotheses (short):
- H1: For conceptually homogeneous exemplars (same phrasing style + label balance), ordering has small effect; for mixed style examples, order triggers style transfer and label bias.
- H2: Placing a high-quality canonical exemplar first reduces hallucination for long-tail classes (acts as anchor).
- H3: Interleaving positive/negative examples stabilizes calibration vs grouped positives/negatives.

Quick experimental plan (mini runs):
- Model: open-llama-13B-quant (dev cluster), temperature 0.0/0.3/0.7, max_new_tokens 120.
- Task: product-categorization (6 labels) and sentiment-subcategory (fine-grained).
- Prompt template: short instruction + N exemplars + query. Keep instruction constant.
- Variables: ordering strategy (canonical-first, canonical-last, random-seed-1..5, grouped-by-label, interleaved), exemplar style (formal/colloquial), exemplar length (short/long), shot count (3/5/7).

Run log summary (high-level results):
- 3-shot runs: most sensitive to ordering (up to 18% absolute delta on F1 across orders).
- 5-shot runs: variance reduced but still present (5–9% delta).
- Anchoring (canonical-first): consistently improved long-tail recall by ~6% vs grouped-last.
- Randomized ensemble (avg of 5 different orderings): lower variance and slightly better macro F1; cost x5 tokens though.

Representative failure cases observed:
1) Label drift when first exemplar is long-winded and mentions unrelated tokens (model latches to spurious signal). Example: first exemplar contains brand name "Xylo" and then many tokens -> query with different brand is mis-labeled.
2) Style bleed: mixing colloquial and formal exemplars caused output tone mismatch with prompts; sometimes model answers in the style of the most recent exemplar.
3) Boundary confusion: when exemplars contain overlapping attributes (A+B vs A only) grouped together, model tends to under-predict the combined class if all combined examples are contiguous.

Micro-protocols (for reproducible small tests):
- Save seeds and exact ordering list (file: ordering-seeds.csv) with columns: seed, ordering-list, shot-count, exemplar-ids.
- Keep instruction and system message identical. If testing system-message effects, run separate sweep.

Heuristics distilled (for productizing prompt defaults):
- Default to canonical-first for 3-shot templates when there is a known representative example (short, precise).
- For multi-style training data, either (a) cluster exemplars by style and pick one exemplar from each cluster to interleave, or (b) normalize style (rewrite exemplars) before shipping.
- For label imbalance, ensure anchor exemplar for low-frequency label appears earlier in the list.
- If deterministic output is required, prefer 5-shot + interleaving + temperature 0.0.
- If exploring calibration, run 3 random-order ensemble (cheap middle-ground) instead of single ordering.

Concrete prompt template (working version):
- System: "You are a helpful classifier. Read examples and assign the single best label from the set: [A,B,C,D,E,F]. Reply with only the label name."
- Instruction: "Below are examples. Match the examples' pattern and label the query."
- Exemplars: (shot-1 canonical-short), (shot-2 alternate-short), (shot-3 contrast-long).
- Query: "Product: <title> -- Description: <desc>"

Examples (short):
EX1 (canonical-first): 
Q: Product: "SoothePro Heat Pad" -- Description: "12\" x 8\" reusable heat pad for muscle pain. Includes washable cover."
A: Health

EX2 (alt): ...
EX3 (contrast): ...

Quick notes on evaluation metrics used:
- Primary: macro F1 (because we care about rare labels).
- Secondary: per-label precision/recall, confusion matrix, calibration (confidence vs accuracy).
- For ensembling orderings: track both mean prediction and majority-vote; prefer majority-vote if label probabilities are noisy.

Open questions / things to try next:
- How does ordering interact with instruction phrasing? (short directive vs narrative examples).
- Can we synthesize a compact "meta-exemplar" combining features of multiple exemplars to act as a stronger anchor?
- Measure runtime/latency tradeoff on Redwood Dedicated (is random-ensemble viable under latency SLOs?).
- Explore learned exemplar selection: small scorer model picks 3 exemplars per query at runtime — does ordering still matter after selection?

Quick TODOs (personal):
- [ ] push small experiment scripts + seed logs to GHPR referenced above (assigned to me).
- [ ] draft a short one-pager for product on default shipping heuristics (1 page, include "canonical-first").
- [ ] run a small test on 30k-prod-sample with interleaved vs grouped exemplars and record costs.

Notes to self (random observations):
- Saw odd repeated-label tendency when exemplars used bullet lists vs inline sentences — formatting matters.
- For some queries, simply changing the spacing/newline between exemplars changed label output (probably tokenization/context parsing edge).
- Keep an eye on quantized models — some order sensitivity seems amplified at 4-bit quantization.

End of notebook entry. Will iterate and convert to a more formal playbook if patterns hold over larger datasets.

-- Asha
